status_note: Reproduces on Spark 4.3.0 in both ANSI modes, interpreted and codegen. SPARK-45438 (open since 2023, Scala 2.13 builds) reports the raise for `-x` and `abs(x)` at the largest 38-digit decimal; the silent rounding of any decimal past 34 significant digits is the same cause and is not in it. Source at v4.3.0 (98bc0212): `Decimal.unary_-` still negates the Scala `BigDecimal`, whose `MathContext` is `DECIMAL128`.
summary: `-x` of a `DECIMAL` with more than 34 significant digits rounds it to 34 digits, half to even, silently: `-CAST('12345678901234567890123456789012345678' AS DECIMAL(38,0))` is -12345678901234567890123456789012350000. `abs(x)` negates a negative `x` the same way and returns a positive one unchanged. `0 - x` is exact up to a scale of 6.

At 10³⁸ - 1 the rounding reaches 10³⁸, which does not fit `DECIMAL(38,0)`, so `-x` raises `NUMERIC_VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE` even with ANSI off. `Decimal.unary_-` (sql/api/.../types/Decimal.scala#L567-L575) builds `-decimalVal` on a Scala `BigDecimal`, which rounds to its default `MathContext.DECIMAL128` (34 digits, `HALF_EVEN`); `abs` calls it for a negative value.
handling: The Spark profile (#739) should spell `negate` of a decimal as `0 - x` and `abs` as `CASE WHEN x < 0 THEN 0 - x ELSE x END`. With precision loss on (the default) `0 - x` of a `DECIMAL(38,s)` drops one digit of scale past `s = 6` (it needs 39 digits), so for those scales the profile needs another spelling or `spark.sql.decimalOperations.allowPrecisionLoss` off. The fix upstream is to negate the Java `BigDecimal` (`decimalVal.underlying.negate()`), which is exact.
found_by: the Spark characterization (#738): sverify_dev.probe_spark, then a manual repro of `decimal-overflow-subtract`

checked.note: probes decimal-negate-34-digits and decimal-negate-max of characterization/spark/probes.json, both ANSI modes, folded and codegen.
